newsitem.title: CANADA: Vancouver bourse shuts down after computer glitch.
newsitem.headline: Vancouver bourse shuts down after computer glitch.

text.p: The Vancouver Stock Exchange said late on Tuesday that technical difficulties had forced the bourse to close its computerized trading at 1107 PDT/1807 GMT for the remainder of the session.
The VSE said the problems were caused by network changes made on the weekend to the VSE's trading system. Initial problems were first detected on Monday but rectified by the exchange.
Tuesday's problems were more serious and forced the close of trading after minimal trading volumes were recorded, the exchange said.
It said trading was expected to resume on Wednesday at 0630 PDT/1330 GMT.

The Toronto Stock Exchange, Canada's largest, was forced to halt trading several times last week after voluminous trade in Bre-X Minerals Ltd caused the TSE's antiquated computer trading system to collapse. The problem was rectified when a section of computer code was rewritten to deal with a high volume of trade.
Tuesday's closure in Vancouver was the first suffered by the exchange, which trades mostly small resource stocks, since an outage last summer. -- Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8100
